cohort: 134 adolescents aged 10-20 years, born between 1992 and 2002 in a capital city in the Brazilian northeast, including those born preterm (<37 weeks gestation) and a matched group born at term
finding: Although preterm birth was not associated with a significant increase in cardiovascular risk factors in this sample of adolescents, preterm females had lower height and waist-hip circumference ratio, while preterm males had lower cesarean delivery rates and greater family history of cardiovascular disease.
mod_finding: Preterm males had lower rates of cesarean delivery compared to term males (p = 0.05).
